subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'The kirana shop makes atta in the back of the shop. Farmers have nothing to do with it.' Fix Golu.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kirana wale dukaan ke peeche atta banate hain. Kisaan ka isse koi lena-dena nahi.' Golu ko theek karo.
answer: Farmers grow the wheat; it is harvested, threshed, cleaned and ground at a mill or chakki; the shop only sells the atta.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why we shouldn't waste food, and give two safe ways to use leftovers.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki khaana kyon bekaar nahi karna chahiye, aur bache khaane ko use karne ke do safe tareeke batao.
answer: Food carries the work of many people plus water, land and fuel; take only what you can eat; turn safely stored leftovers into new dishes (lemon rice, roti upma, dal paratha); never eat spoiled food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: what happens at the chakki?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: chakki mein kya hota hai?
answer: Wheat grains are ground into flour (atta).

subject: evs
prompt_en: A big watermelon is much heavier than a small coin. Predict: which one will float in a big tub of water?
prompt_hi: Bada tarbooz chhote sikke se kahin zyada bhaari hai. Guess karo: paani ke bade tub mein kaun tairega?
answer: The watermelon floats; the coin sinks.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Roll some modelling clay into a tight ball and put it in water: it sinks. Predict: if you press the same clay into a thin bowl or boat shape and place it gently on the water, will it float?
prompt_hi: Modelling clay ki kas ke goli banao aur paani mein daalo: woh doob jaati hai. Guess karo: agar usi clay ko daba ke patli katori ya naav bana do aur dheere se paani pe rakho, toh kya tairegi?
answer: Yes, it can float: the boat shape pushes aside more water, so the water's upward push is enough to hold it up.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put an orange with its peel on into water, then the same orange after peeling it. Predict which one floats.
prompt_hi: Chhilke wala santra paani mein daalo, phir wahi santra chheel ke daalo. Guess karo kaun tairega.
answer: The orange with its peel floats; the peeled orange sinks. The peel is full of tiny air pockets that help it float.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A potato sinks in a glass of tap water. Predict: if we stir lots and lots of salt (many spoons) into the water, what will happen to the potato?
prompt_hi: Aloo saade paani ke glass mein doob jaata hai. Guess karo: agar us paani mein bahut saara namak (kai chammach) ghol dein, toh aloo ka kya hoga?
answer: It can float: very salty water pushes up harder than plain water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why does a huge iron ship float while a tiny iron nail sinks?
prompt_hi: Bahut bada lohe ka jahaaz tairta hai, par chhoti si lohe ki keel doob jaati hai. Aisa kyon?
answer: The ship is hollow, shaped like a giant bowl and full of air, so it pushes aside a huge amount of water and the water's upward push holds it up; the nail is solid and pushes aside only a little water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A steel katori placed upright floats on water, but a steel spoon sinks. Both are steel. What is different?
prompt_hi: Steel ki katori seedhi rakhne pe paani pe tairti hai, par steel ka chammach doob jaata hai. Dono steel ke hain. Farak kya hai?
answer: The katori's hollow bowl shape pushes aside lots of water and holds air; the spoon is thin and solid and pushes aside very little water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Fishing boats in Kerala are often made of wood, but big cargo ships are made of steel. How can a steel boat float?
prompt_hi: Kerala ki machhli pakadne wali naavein aksar lakdi ki hoti hain, par bade cargo jahaaz steel ke. Steel ki naav kaise tairti hai?
answer: It is shaped hollow like a bowl, so it pushes aside a lot of water and floats, just like the clay boat.

subject: evs
prompt_en: People say it is easier to float in the sea than in a river or swimming pool. Why might that be?
prompt_hi: Log kehte hain ki samandar mein nadi ya swimming pool se zyada aasaani se tair-te hain. Aisa kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: Sea water is salty, and salty water pushes up harder, so we float more easily.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Look at this picture of two tubs with the same lump of clay: in tub A it is a ball at the bottom; in tub B it is a boat floating. In which tub has the water level risen more? Say it in words.
prompt_hi: Ye picture dekho, do tub mein ek jaisi clay: tub A mein goli neeche padi hai, tub B mein naav tair rahi hai. Kis tub mein paani ka level zyada upar aaya? Shabdon mein batao.
answer: Tub B: the floating boat pushes aside more water, so the water level rises more.

subject: evs
prompt_en: When you push an empty, closed bottle under water, you feel it pushing back on your hand, and when you let go it jumps up. What is pushing it?
prompt_hi: Jab khaali band bottle ko paani mein neeche dabaate ho, toh woh haath ko wapas dhakelti hai, aur chhodte hi upar uchhal aati hai. Use kaun dhakel raha hai?
answer: The water is pushing up on the bottle; the bottle is very light for its size, so the water's upward push is bigger than its weight.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Heavy things sink and light things float. That's the rule!' Give one example that breaks Golu's rule.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Bhaari cheezein doobti hain aur halki tairti hain. Yahi rule hai!' Ek example do jo Golu ka rule tod de.
answer: A heavy log, watermelon or ship floats; a light coin, pin or pebble sinks. Weight alone doesn't decide.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu how a boat made of clay can float even though a ball of the same clay sinks.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki clay ki naav kaise tair sakti hai jabki usi clay ki goli doob jaati hai.
answer: It is the same clay with the same weight, but the hollow boat shape pushes aside much more water; water pushes up on it more, enough to hold it up.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name one heavy thing that floats and one light thing that sinks.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek bhaari cheez batao jo tairti hai, aur ek halki jo doobti hai.
answer: Heavy that floats: a log, a watermelon, a ship, a coconut. Light that sinks: a coin, a pin, a pebble, a nail.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Make a paper helicopter: take a strip of paper, tear it halfway down the middle to make two wings, fold one wing forward and one back, and fold the bottom up a little. Stand on the floor and drop it from as high as you can reach. What does it do?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz ka helicopter banao: kaagaz ki ek patti lo, beech se aadhe tak phaado taaki do pankh banein, ek pankh aage aur ek peeche modo, aur neeche ka hissa thoda upar mod do. Zameen pe khade hokar jitna upar haath jaaye wahan se girao. Kya hota hai?
answer: It spins round and round as it falls slowly; the air pushes on its wings and turns it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Clip a paper clip to the bottom of your paper helicopter. Predict: will it fall faster or slower than before?
prompt_hi: Apne kaagaz ke helicopter ke neeche ek paper clip laga do. Guess karo: pehle se tez girega ya dheere?
answer: Faster: the extra weight pulls it down harder compared with the air pushing up on the wings.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Make one helicopter with long wings and one with short wings from the same paper. Predict which one falls more slowly.
prompt_hi: Ek hi kaagaz se do helicopter banao, ek lambe pankh wala aur ek chhote pankh wala. Guess karo kaun dheere girega.
answer: The long-winged one: bigger wings catch more air, so it falls more slowly.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Roll the same ball with the same push on a smooth floor and on a carpet or durrie. Predict where it will go farther.
prompt_hi: Ek hi ball ko ek jaise dhakke se chikne farsh pe aur carpet ya dari pe ludhkao. Guess karo kahan zyada door jayegi.
answer: On the smooth floor: the carpet rubs against the ball more (more friction) and slows it down sooner.

subject: evs
prompt_en: You run with a phirki, first slowly and then fast. Predict: when will it spin faster?
prompt_hi: Tum phirki leke daudte ho, pehle dheere phir tez. Guess karo: kab zyada tez ghoomegi?
answer: When you run fast: more air pushes on the blades, so it spins faster.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why doesn't a phirki spin when you hold it still in a closed room?
prompt_hi: Band kamre mein phirki ko seedha pakad ke khade raho toh woh kyon nahi ghoomti?
answer: There is no moving air to push its blades; it needs a push from wind to turn.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Drop a flat sheet of paper and a crumpled ball made from an identical sheet at the same time. Which lands first, and what is different about them?
prompt_hi: Ek seedhi kaagaz ki sheet aur usi jaisi sheet ko mod ke banayi goli, dono ek saath girao. Pehle kaun girta hai, aur dono mein kya farak hai?
answer: The crumpled ball lands first; both weigh the same, but the flat sheet has a big surface that the air pushes against, which slows it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Button spinner: pass a string through two holes of a big button, twist the string, then pull the ends in and out. What makes the button spin?
prompt_hi: Button spinner: bade button ke do chhedon mein dhaaga daalo, dhaage ko ghuma ke lapeto, phir dono sire kheencho aur dheela chhodo. Button ko kaun ghuma raha hai?
answer: Your pulls on the string: as the twisted string is pulled tight it unwinds and spins the button, and the button's spin winds it up again for the next pull.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Windmills on hills in Tamil Nadu and Gujarat turn their huge blades. What pushes them, and why are they built in windy places?
prompt_hi: Tamil Nadu aur Gujarat ki pahaadiyon pe bade-bade windmill ke pankh ghoomte hain. Unhe kaun ghumata hai, aur unhe hawa wali jagah pe kyon lagaate hain?
answer: The wind pushes the blades, like a giant phirki; windy places give stronger, steadier pushes, so the blades turn more and make more electricity.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Here is a table: Spinner A (short wings) took 1 second to fall; Spinner B (long wings) took 3 seconds. Tell me in words what this shows.
prompt_hi: Ye table dekho: Spinner A (chhote pankh) ko girne mein 1 second laga; Spinner B (lambe pankh) ko 3 second. Shabdon mein batao ye kya dikhata hai.
answer: The long-winged spinner fell more slowly (it took longer), because longer wings catch more air.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'My lattu stopped because the push I gave it got used up inside it.' What's a better explanation?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mera lattu isliye ruk gaya kyonki maine jo dhakka diya tha woh uske andar khatam ho gaya.' Isse behtar explanation kya hai?
answer: The floor and the air rub against the spinning lattu (friction), slowing it down until it stops.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu how a phirki works and how to make it spin faster.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki phirki kaise kaam karti hai aur use aur tez kaise ghuma sakte hain.
answer: Moving air pushes on the bent blades and turns them; more or faster air (running faster, stronger wind) means a faster spin; with no wind it doesn't spin.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: what must happen for anything to start moving?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kisi bhi cheez ko chalna shuru karne ke liye kya hona zaroori hai?
answer: It must be pushed or pulled.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put the paper-making steps in order: drying, making pulp, pressing out water, spreading the pulp thin.
prompt_hi: Kaagaz banane ke steps kram mein lagao: sukhaana, pulp banana, paani nichodna, pulp ko patla phailaana.
answer: making pulp → spreading the pulp thin → pressing out the water → drying

subject: evs
prompt_en: Slowly tear a piece of newspaper and look closely at the torn edge (with a magnifying glass if you have one). Predict first: will the edge be smooth or hairy?
prompt_hi: Akhbaar ka ek tukda dheere se phaado aur phati hui kinaari ko dhyaan se dekho (magnifying glass ho toh usse). Pehle guess karo: kinaari chikni hogi ya roeydaar?
answer: Hairy or fuzzy: you can see tiny fibres from plants, which is what paper is made of.

subject: evs
prompt_en: We soak torn newspaper in a bucket of water overnight. Predict what it will be like in the morning.
prompt_hi: Phate hue akhbaar ko raat bhar paani ki baalti mein bhigo dete hain. Guess karo subah woh kaisa hoga?
answer: Soft, mushy and falling apart: the fibres loosen in water, so it can be mashed into pulp.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict: which uses more trees and water, making 100 notebooks from fresh wood or making 100 notebooks from old paper?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: kismein zyada ped aur paani lagta hai, nayi lakdi se 100 copy banane mein ya purane kaagaz se 100 copy banane mein?
answer: From fresh wood: recycling old paper saves trees and uses less water and energy.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do we press and dry the pulp when making paper?
prompt_hi: Kaagaz banate waqt pulp ko dabaate aur sukhaate kyon hain?
answer: To squeeze out the water so the fibres stick together tightly into a thin, flat, strong sheet.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a leaf and a sheet of paper. Both come from plants. How are they different?
prompt_hi: Ek patte aur ek kaagaz ki sheet ki tulna karo. Dono paudhon se aate hain. Farak kya hai?
answer: A leaf grows on a plant by itself; paper is made by people from plant fibres that are broken up, mixed with water, spread, pressed and dried.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your class uses a lot of paper. Name three ways to waste less paper at school.
prompt_hi: Tumhari class bahut kaagaz use karti hai. School mein kaagaz kam bekaar karne ke 3 tareeke batao.
answer: Any three: use both sides, use old notebooks for rough work, put used paper in a recycling bin, practise on slates or whiteboards, don't tear pages out.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In India some paper is made from bagasse, the dry leftover after sugarcane juice is squeezed out. Why is that a smart idea?
prompt_hi: India mein kuch kaagaz bagasse se banta hai, jo ganne ka ras nikaalne ke baad bacha hua sookha hissa hai. Ye samajhdaari kyon hai?
answer: It uses a waste material instead of cutting trees, so trees are saved and something that would be thrown away becomes useful.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Four pictures are out of order: a sheet drying in the sun; torn newspaper in a bucket of water; mushy pulp spread on a net; a cloth pressing out water. Put them in order and say each step.
prompt_hi: Chaar picture ulte-seedhe hain: dhoop mein sookhti sheet; paani ki baalti mein phata akhbaar; jaali pe phaila hua gila pulp; kapde se paani nichodna. Inhe kram mein lagao aur har step bolo.
answer: Torn paper soaked in water → pulp spread on the net → pressed with a cloth to squeeze out water → dried in the sun.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Paper grows on paper trees, and people just pluck the sheets.' What's the mistake?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kaagaz ke ped pe kaagaz ugte hain, log bas sheet tod lete hain.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Paper doesn't grow; people make it from plant fibres (like wood or bamboo) by making pulp, spreading it, pressing it and drying it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu how to make recycled paper at home from old newspapers, step by step, using only safe things.
prompt_hi: Golu ko step-by-step samjhao ki ghar pe purane akhbaar se recycled kaagaz kaise banate hain, sirf safe cheezon se.
answer: Tear the paper into bits, soak it in water overnight, mash it with your hands into pulp, spread it thinly on a net or cloth, press out the water with another cloth, and dry it in the sun.
